subject: Amendment to Certification
title: PERC AC-2015-002 Final Order (Amendment to Certification)

STATE OF FLORIDA
PUBLIC EMPLOYEES RELATIONS COMMISSION
IN RE
PETITION OF WILLIAM NICHOLS Case No. AC- 2015 -002
LODGE #8 (MIAMI BEACH),
FRATERNAL ORDER OF POLICE, ORDER AMENDING
:
TO AMEND CERTIFICATION NO. 345. CERTIFICATION NO. 345
:
Order Number: 15E -285
Date Issued: September 17, 2015
Kathleen M. Phillips, Miami, attorney for William Nichols Lodge #8 (Miami Beach),
Fraternal Order of Police.
Raul J. Aguila, Miami Beach, attorney for City of Miami Beach.
On August 3, 2015, the William Nichols Lodge #8 (Miami Beach), Fraternal Order
of Police (Lodge #8), filed an amendment to certification petition seeking to substitute
itself for the Florida State Lodge, Fraternal Order of Police, Inc. (FOP), as the certified
bargaining representative for a unit of rank -and -file law enforcement personnel employed
by the City of Miami Beach (City). See Florida State Lodge, Fraternal Order of Police v.
City of Miami Beach, Case No. 8H -RC- 766 -2085 (Fla. PERC Aug. 12, 1977)
(Certification 345). On August 6, a hearing officer was assigned to the case.
The hearing officer directed the City to file a response to the petition and advised
the City that, if it did not file a response, he would assume that the petition did not raise
disputed issues of material fact and that the City did not object to the granting of the
petition. The City did not file a response to the petition.
On August 31, the hearing officer issued an order recommending that the petition
be granted. Neither party filed exceptions to the hearing officer's order. Upon

AC-2015-002
consideration, and for the reasons articulated by the hearing officer, Lodge #8's petition
is GRANTED and Certification 345 is amended to reflect the William Nichols Lodge #8
(Miami Beach), Fraternal Order of Police, as the certified bargaining agent.
This order may be appealed to the appropriate district court of appeal. A notice of
appeal must be received by the Commission and the district court of appeal within thirty
days from the date of this order. Except in cases of indigency, the court will require a
filing fee and the Commission will require payment for preparing the record on appeal.
Further explanation of the right to appeal is provided in Sections 120.68 and 447.504,
Florida Statutes (2015), and the Florida Rules of Appellate Procedure.
It is so ordered.
DELGADO and POOLE, Commissioners, concur.

STATE OF FLORIDA
PUBLIC EMPLOYEES RELATIONS COMMISSION
IN RE
PETITION OF WILLIAM NICHOLS Case No. AC- 2015 -002
LODGE #8 (MIAMI BEACH),
FRATERNAL ORDER OF POLICE, HEARING OFFICER'S
:
TO AMEND CERTIFICATION NO. 345. RECOMMENDED ORDER
:
Kathleen M. Phillips, Miami, attorney for William Nichols Lodge #8 (Miami Beach),
Fraternal Order of Police.
Raul J. Aguila, Miami Beach, attorney for City of Miami Beach.
RIX, Hearing Officer.
On August 3, 2015, the William Nichols Lodge #8 (Miami Beach), Fraternal Order
of Police (Lodge #8), filed an amendment to certification petition pursuant to Section
447.207(6), Florida Statutes (2015).1 The petition seeks to amend certification 345 to
reflect Florida State Lodge, Fraternal Order of Police, Inc.'s (Florida State Lodge)
designation of Lodge #8 as the certified bargaining representative of a bargaining unit of
City of Miami Beach (City) rank -and -file law enforcement personnel. See Florida State
Lodge, Fraternal Order of Police v. City of Miami Beach, Case No. 8H -RC- 766 -2085 (Fla.
PERC Aug. 12, 1977) (designating Florida State Lodge as the certified bargaining
representative of the City's rank- and -file law enforcement personnel). On August 6, the
Commission appointed the undersigned as hearing officer in this case.
'The Petitioner's name has been amended to conform to the name in which it is
currently registered. See In Re William Nichols Lodge #8 (Miami Beach), Fraternal Order
of Police, (Fla. PERC, July 31, 2015).

AC-2015-002
On August 14, I directed the City to file a response to the petition by the close of
business on August 24 and serve a copy on Lodge #8. I notified the City that if it did not
file a response, I would assume that the petition does not raise disputed issues of
material fact and that the City does not oppose the granting of the petition. To date, no
response has been filed.
The Commission has approved amendments of certification to substitute a local
union for its parent organization when two criteria are met: (1) the union demonstrates
that there will be substantial continuity in the representation of the members of the
bargaining unit and (2) the substitution has been approved by the members of the
bargaining unit. See In re Gator Lodge 67, Inc., Fraternal Order of Police to Amend
Certification No. 1053, 31 FPER 132 (2005); In re Fraternal Order of Police, Clearwater
Lodge #10, Inc., to Amend Certification No. 239, 29 FPER 92 (2003). Such approval is
evidenced by a showing that all members of the bargaining unit were provided with:
(a) reasonable notice of the proposed change, (b) a reasonable opportunity for
discussion of the change prior to a vote, and (c) a voting procedure which fairly reflects
the employees' desires. See In re Rockledge Professional Firefighters Association,
15 FPER ¶ 20195 (1989).
As noted above, the Florida State Lodge was originally certified by the
Commission in 1977 as the exclusive bargaining agent of the regular full -time and regular
part-time sworn lieutenants and lower- ranking police personnel. According to the petition
2

AC-2015-002
and supporting documentation, Lodge #8 is a subordinate lodge of the Florida State
Lodge, and is a labor organization. The Florida State Lodge has designated Lodge #8 to
negotiate and administer a succession of collective bargaining agreements and to be
otherwise responsible for representing the bargaining unit with respect to rates of pay,
benefits, and terms and conditions of employment.
For over thirty years Lodge #8 has been the de facto bargaining representative for
the bargaining unit through its officers, committees, and designees. Lodge #8 has
maintained control of the bargaining unit's finances. It collects, maintains, and expends
all bargaining unit monies, including membership dues. It has negotiated and executed
collective bargaining agreements and administered those agreements, including the
current agreement, with the City. Lodge #8 has provided representation to bargaining
unit employees for processing all grievances, representing them in internal affairs,
investigations, and disciplinary matters. The City has been negotiating with Lodge #8 in
regards to the unit for over thirty years and has recognized Lodge #8 as the certified
bargaining agent.
Lodge #8 is governed by the same constitution and by -laws of its parent
organization, the Florida State Lodge. The proposed amendment to substitute the
certification from the Florida State Lodge to its subordinate Lodge #8 will not change the
manner in which business has been conducted regarding rates of pay, benefits, and all
terms and conditions of employment for bargaining unit employees and there will be
substantial continuity in the representation of the bargaining unit employees because
3

AC-2015-002
Lodge #8 will continue to negotiate and administer the collective bargaining agreements
and represent bargaining unit employees in grievances and disciplinary matters. The
same officers will be conducting business on behalf of the bargaining unit.
The proposed amendment will formalize the de facto bargaining representative
status of Lodge #8. None of the bargaining unit members will have any diminution in
rights as a result of substituting the parent organization, Florida State Lodge, with
Lodge #8 and it will continue representing bargaining unit members in the identical
fashion.
The national and state lodges' constitutions provide for the chartering of
subordinate lodges such as Lodge #8. The establishment and transfer of responsibilities
from the national and state lodges to subordinate lodges is contemplated by and
accomplished in accordance with constitutional provisions adopted by the membership,
including the membership of Lodge #8. The governing documents do not require notice
and a vote to approve the substitution, as this is a change involving internal union
matters with no impact upon the representational or membership interests or rights of
bargaining unit employees. The amendment to certification is a formalization of rights
and responsibilities already performed by Lodge #8.
Based upon the undisputed facts, I conclude that Lodge #8 has met the first prong
of the test by demonstrating that there will be substantial continuity in the representation
of the members of the bargaining unit. The undisputed evidence shows that Lodge #8
has been the de facto bargaining agent for the affected employees through its
4

AC-2015-002
negotiation of collective bargaining agreements, representation of bargaining unit
employees in grievance and disciplinary matters, and in executing the collective
bargaining agreements for the affected employees. It will continue these functions
should the petition be granted. The practical effect of the proposed amendment is to
formalize the de facto bargaining representative status of Lodge #8.
As to the second prong of the test I note that there is no evidence presented
showing approval by the bargaining unit members through notice of the proposed
change, a reasonable opportunity for discussion of the change, and a voting procedure
which fairly reflects the employees' desires. However, the national and state lodge
constitutions authorize the chartering of subordinate lodges, and the establishment and
transfer of responsibilities from the national and state lodges is contemplated by and
accomplished in accordance with constitutional provisions adopted by the membership.
These provisions do not require notice and a vote to approve substitutions under the
circumstances herein.
Therefore, the absence of notice and a vote should not be fatal to the petition
under the circumstances herein. See, e.q., In re Gator Lodge 67, Inc., Fraternal Order of
Police to Amend Certification No. 1053, 31 FPER at 299 (2005); In re Fraternal Order of
Police, Clearwater Lodge #10, Inc., 29 FPER at 236. Based on the foregoing, I
recommend that the Commission grant the instant petition and amend certification 345
reflect the substitution of Lodge #8 for the Florida State Lodge as the certified bargaining
representative.
5

AC-2015-002
Any party may file exceptions to my recommended order, but exceptions must be
received by the Commission within fifteen days from the date of this order. See Fla.
Admin. Code Rule 28- 106.217(1). An extension of time for filing exceptions will not be
granted unless good cause is shown.
